feedback: Approve this single-variable test. The candidate is the iteration 5 design (score 403.4, best raced so far) with sensor row y moved from 0.05 m to 0.03 m. Sensor x, sensor_size 0.016, kp 2.6, kd 0.6, ki 0.1 and base_speed 1.2 are unchanged. The change follows from iteration 6, which showed that sensor_size 0.012 lowered the score to 302.6 and raised s-bend off-track endings, so the 0.012 direction is closed. Iteration 5 still had oval oscillation at 0.219, s-bend at 0.260 and slalom at 0.192, all of which point to a sensing-to-steering lag rather than more damping. Iteration 4 showed that kd 0.45 to 0.6 helped the oval but raised s-bend and slalom oscillation, so further kd is not the lever. The ±0.07 m span stays, because iteration 4 showed it removes most line loss (0.15 on the oval, 0.0 on the s-bend and slalom). The candidate is valid: all y values are within -0.06 to 0.08, the x values are within range, sensor_size 0.016 is allowed, and the controller values are inside their limits. Nothing is obviously broken. The main risk is that less look-ahead raises max_error on the tighter bends, and the outer sensors may see less tape. I cannot say how it will perform. With four iterations left after this one, racing a clean one-variable step gives more useful telemetry than another reading-only round. Next race, read the results as follows. If steering_oscillation falls below 0.2 on the oval and s-bend, and line_loss_events stays near 0 with s-bend max_error under 0.06, keep y at 0.03 and raise base_speed to 1.3 (then 1.4), with kp and kd fixed, to test completion_time under 3 s. If line_loss_events rises above about 0.3 on any track, or s-bend max_error rises above 0.065, return y to 0.05 (iteration 5 geometry) before testing anything else. If slalom steering_oscillation rises well above its iteration 5 level of 0.192, return kd to about 0.5.
